# Detection Principles {#principles-section}

## Transparent Universe, opaque Earth {#interaction-probability}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### Across the Universe

**A $1\,\mathrm{PeV}$ muon neutrino in today's mean baryonic matter**

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
$$
\bar n_{b,0}\simeq0.25\,\mathrm{m^{-3}}
=2.5\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}
$$

$$
\sigma_{\nu N}^{\mathrm{CC+NC}}
\simeq9.5\times10^{-34}\,\mathrm{cm^2}
$$

About one nucleon per four cubic metres.
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
$$
\lambda_{\nu N,0}=\frac{1}{\bar n_{b,0}\sigma_{\nu N}}
\simeq4.2\times10^{39}\,\mathrm{cm}
$$

$$
\lambda_{\nu N,0}\simeq4.4\times10^{21}\,\mathrm{ly}
$$

Observable diameter today: $D_{\rm obs}\simeq93\times10^9\,\mathrm{ly}$.
:::
:::::

$$
\frac{\lambda_{\nu N,0}}{D_{\rm obs}}\simeq5\times10^{10}
$$

::: {.media-caption}
Present-epoch $\nu N$ estimate ignoring the Universe evolution.
[PDG baryon density](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2025/reviews/rpp2024-rev-astrophysical-constants.pdf);
[CSMS cross sections, Table I](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.3723).
:::

### Through the Earth

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="65%"}
![](media/propagation/earth-transport-full-dark.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 540px;" fig-alt="Ratio of the neutrino flux reaching a detector 1 km deep to the flux entering the Earth, versus zenith angle from 90 to 180 degrees and energy from 10 GeV to 100 PeV, with neutral-current regeneration. Near the horizon the Earth is transparent at all energies; through the centre half of the flux survives up to about 20 TeV and 10 percent up to about 170 TeV. Dashed contours without regeneration lie slightly lower in energy."}

::: {.media-caption}
Full transport: V. A. Allakhverdyan (CT10nlo, PREM, detector 1 km deep), redrawn ·
[V. A. Allakhverdyan, dissertation (2026), Fig. 4.20](https://issc.jinr.ru/files/326/f_2_5830.pdf) · [Allakhverdyan, Zavyalov & Naumov (2026), Fig. 9](https://www1.jinr.ru/Pepan_letters/panl_2026_2/05_Allahverd_rus.pdf)
:::
:::
::: {.column width="31%"}
$$
1\,\mathrm{PeV}=10^6\,\mathrm{GeV}
$$

**Horizontal axis:** zenith angle.

$90^\circ$: near the horizon.

$180^\circ$: through Earth's centre.

**Colour:** flux at the detector over flux entering the Earth.

**Dashed:** without regeneration,

$$
e^{-N_A\,\sigma_{\rm tot}(E)\,X(\theta)}.
$$

::: {.small}
Neutral currents do not remove a neutrino; they move it to lower energy. With regeneration the ratio depends on the incident spectrum.
:::
:::
:::::

### Diameter estimate

$$
\lambda_{\nu N}(\rho)=\frac{1}{N_A\rho\sigma_{\nu N}}
\simeq3.2\times10^3\,\mathrm{km}
\left(\frac{5.5\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}}{\rho}\right).
$$

Earth's diameter is $12742\,\mathrm{km}$; its dense core matters.

$$
X_{\rm diam}=\int_{\rm diameter}\rho(\ell)\,d\ell
\simeq1.1\times10^{10}\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-2}}
\quad\text{(PREM)}.
$$

$$
\tau_{\rm diam}=N_A\sigma_{\nu N}X_{\rm diam}\simeq6.3,
\qquad
P_0=e^{-\tau_{\rm diam}}\simeq1.8\times10^{-3}\simeq0.2\%.
$$

- Almost no PeV neutrinos cross the full diameter without interacting.
- Near the horizon, the path is much shorter.

::: {.media-caption}
$P_0$: zero CC or NC interactions, not the regenerated flux fraction $\mathcal T$.
[PREM column depth: Gandhi et al.](https://lss.fnal.gov/archive/1995/pub/Pub-95-221-T.pdf)
:::

### Tomography

**One year of IceCube up-going muons weighs the Earth**

- IC86, 2011–2012: 20 145 up-going muons, 0.4–20 TeV; the zenith distribution follows absorption in the Earth.
- Earth's mass: $M_\oplus^\nu=6.0^{+1.6}_{-1.3}\times10^{24}\,\mathrm{kg}$; gravity gives $5.9722\times10^{24}\,\mathrm{kg}$.
- Core mass: $M_{\rm core}^\nu=2.72^{+0.97}_{-0.89}\times10^{24}\,\mathrm{kg}$.
- Moment of inertia: $(6.9\pm2.4)\times10^{37}\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2}$; gravity gives $8.017\times10^{37}$.
- The core is denser than the mantle: a denser mantle has $p=0.011$.

::: {.takeaway}
Weak interactions alone, without gravity, see the Earth's dense core.
:::

::: {.media-caption}
68% credible intervals, default atmospheric-flux model · A. Donini, S. Palomares-Ruiz, J. Salvado, *Nature Physics* **15**, 37 (2019), [arXiv:1803.05901](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.05901)
:::

### Core contrast

![](media/propagation/earth-tomography-contrast-dark.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 430px;" fig-alt="Left: CC survival probability against zenith angle at 10, 30 and 100 TeV for PREM (solid) and a homogeneous Earth of the same mass (dashed); paths through the core are darker in PREM. Right: relative difference between PREM and the homogeneous Earth over energy and zenith angle."}

- Same mass, different profile: PREM against a homogeneous Earth of $5.51\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$.
- Paths through the core (beyond $147^\circ$) lose $\sim20\%$ more neutrinos at $30\,\mathrm{TeV}$; mantle paths lose fewer.

::: {.media-caption}
Computed: PREM, CSMS cross sections, detector 1 km deep · CC absorption only; NC and $\tau$ regeneration not included
:::
::::::
